Zhang, Y., Dube, M.A., McLean, D.D. and Kates, M. (2003). Biodiesel production from waste cooking oil: 1. Process design and technological assessment. Bioresource Technology 89(1), 1-16. doi:10.1016/S0960-8524(03)00040-3

Locator: printed journal page (1-16; PDF page = printed page) and table/figure. Technology paper behind the economics companion zhang_2003_001 (Part 2); same four HYSYS designs at 8000 t/yr (I alkali virgin canola oil; II alkali waste oil with acid esterification pretreatment; III acid waste oil; IV acid with hexane extraction) and the same technology names. Loaded: whole-plant process heat per t biodiesel = sum of column reboiler duties (Table 2) plus utility heaters printed in kJ/h on the flowsheets (Figs. 2-5, read from page images, printed labels not chart readings), divided by the printed FAME stream 401; T-201 methanol-column duty separately; flows per t biodiesel from the stream tables (oil, fresh methanol, catalyst, glycerine solvent, 85% glycerine by-product, wash water). Other-values: condenser and cooler duties, interchanger duties, waste streams, reactor volumes, unit counts. TRAPS: (1) Table 2 labels duties 'MJ' with no time basis; interpreted as 10^6 kJ/h (GJ/h), verified against the printed vapour flow x methanol latent heat for T-201 (Process III 4780 kg/h -> 5.3); if the label meant MJ/h the values would be 1000x smaller and physically impossible. (2) Process II T-101 (pretreatment methanol column) reboiler duty not printed, so Process II heat is understated. (3) E-100 (II) and E-101 (III) are feed/effluent interchangers, not utility heat. (4) Process I: Table 2 says T-501 N/A under NRTL but Fig. 2 still draws it with stream 502. (5) Electricity (pumps) and reactor duties not printed. Only NRTL results given numerically; UNIQUAC raises T-401 load (qualitative). Results compare with West 2008 acid route steam 7.37 GJ/t (this paper 7.9 GJ/t for Process III).
